(b) The nation has become self-sufficient in food and has made great progress in science and technology and in industrialisation.

(d) For a society to grow, it must view the problems of all its people with empathy, solve the problems of economic disparity and injustice, enlarge mass consciousness, promote a true sense of history instead of blind belief in myths, and begin participatory decision-making.

(ii) Demolish: to pull down or destroy completely.

answers.solution:
Title: Good Manners Reveal Character

Small actions, like light through tiny holes, reveal a person's character, which is built from little deeds done well and honestly every day. A chief test of character is how we treat others. Polite behaviour towards everyone shows respect and pleases others, but it pleases us far more. Anyone, rich or poor, can train himself to be courteous and kind. Gentleness, like silent light, is more powerful and fruitful than loud force.

(72 words)

answers.solution:
Note: the poem is misprinted in places. A line introducing 'one sheep' before 'That had no fear of man or sea' is missing, and the last lines ('Eight raged sheep men-tramps / Training and thieves') are garbled; they mean 'Eight ragged sheep-men, tramps and thieves'. The answers follow the sense of the poem.

(a) The poet started from Baltimore with two thousand sheep ('twice a thousand head of sheep').

(b) In the beginning the sheep would not eat or drink, and kept bleating over the sea. Many of them were dying, so every day the men had to sort the living from the dead.

(c) By the time they reached the mouth of the Mersey, five hundred sheep had died.

(d) The sheep was waiting to be stroked. It was a tame sheep that wanted love and care, so it pushed its pleading face through the bars, like a child's pet that had lost its owner.

(e) It was particular because, unlike the others, it was tame and had no fear of man or sea. It struck its pleading face through the bars to be stroked, and the poet felt it was a child's lost pet. Even the rough sheep-men stroked its black nose every time they passed.

(f) (i) A place where sheep are kept: pens
(ii) Shepherds: sheep-men

answers.solution:
Topics attempted: (b) and (c).

(b) Television Is Rightly Called an Idiot Box

Television is a wonderful invention, but today it is often called an idiot box, and the name is not wrong. Many children and adults sit before it for hours, watching silly serials, endless advertisements and noisy shows without thinking. They stop reading, playing outdoors and talking with their families. Too much television harms the eyes, makes people lazy and dulls the mind, because the viewer only receives and never thinks. Yet the fault lies with us, not with the machine. News, nature films and educational programmes can teach us a great deal. If we choose wisely and watch for a limited time, television becomes a window to the world instead of an idiot box.

(c) A Bird in Hand Is Worth Two in the Bush

This proverb means that what we already have is more valuable than something bigger that we only hope to get. The bird in the hand is sure, while the two in the bush may fly away at any moment. Many people lose what they have by chasing larger but uncertain gains. A man may leave a steady job for a dream of quick riches and end up with nothing. The greedy dog in the fable dropped its bone to snatch the bigger bone it saw in the water, and lost both. We should certainly be ambitious, but we must never risk what is certain for what is doubtful.

answers.label: Q.5
answers.solution:
A Cleanliness Drive in Name Only

The picture shows a building with a big board that reads 'Cleanliness Drive'. One would expect the place to be spotless, but the ground in front of it is covered with heaps of garbage, waste paper and dirt. Two men, perhaps the people in charge of the drive, stand right in the middle of the mess, smiling happily as if all is well.

Nearby sit three monkeys, like Gandhiji's famous three monkeys. But instead of 'See no evil, hear no evil, speak no evil', the boards below them read 'See no dirt', 'Smell no dirt' and 'Touch no dirt'.

The cartoonist is making fun of the way many cleanliness drives are carried out. A banner is put up and photographs are taken, but the real work of cleaning is never done. Like the three monkeys, people simply shut their eyes and noses to the filth around them and refuse to touch it.

The message is clear. Cleanliness cannot come through banners and slogans alone. Every citizen must pick up a broom, keep his surroundings clean and refuse to ignore dirt. Only then will a clean India become a reality.

The Editor
The Hindu
Chennai

Subject: Importance of co-curricular activities in the all-round development of students

Sir,

Through the columns of your esteemed newspaper, I wish to express my views on the importance of co-curricular activities in schools.

Education does not mean only reading books and passing examinations. A student also needs a healthy body, a confident mind and good values. Co-curricular activities such as sports, debates, music, dramatics, art, NCC and scouting help to build these qualities. Games teach team spirit, discipline and the ability to accept defeat gracefully. Debates and dramatics remove stage fear and improve speaking skills. Art and music develop creativity, while NCC and scouting teach leadership and service to others.

Sadly, many schools and parents still treat these activities as a waste of time and push children only towards marks. This produces students who may score well but lack confidence and practical skills.

I request schools to make co-curricular activities a regular part of the timetable, and parents to encourage their children to take part in them. Only then will our students grow into well-rounded citizens.

Yours faithfully,
Manoj Pandey

answers.solution:
Man Is the Most Dangerous Animal in the World

Good morning, respected Principal, teachers and my dear friends. Today I am going to speak on the topic 'Man is the most dangerous animal in the world'.

We fear lions, tigers and snakes. But a tiger kills only when it is hungry, and a snake bites only when it is attacked. Man, on the other hand, harms others out of greed, anger and pride.

Man has cut down forests, polluted rivers and the air, and driven many animals to extinction. He has made guns, bombs and nuclear weapons that can destroy the whole world in minutes. Wars, terrorism and crime are all his work.

Yet man is also the only animal blessed with reason and a conscience. If he chooses, he can use his intelligence to protect nature and live in peace. Let us promise to be kind to all living beings and make our planet a safer place.

Thank you.

answers.finalAnswer: The chair is made of wood.; The number of board members is very small.; She is the cleverest girl in the class.; We don't agree with what Mr Sharma says.; He wishes the train would move faster.
answers.solution:
(a) The chair is made of wood. (A material noun takes no article.)

(b) The number of board members is very small. ('The number' is singular.)

(c) She is the cleverest girl in the class. ('Most' and '-est' are never used together, and we say 'in the class'.)

(d) We don't agree with what Mr Sharma says. (We agree 'with' a person or opinion, and 'to' a proposal.)

(e) He wishes the train would move faster. (After 'wish', a present wish takes a past form; 'He wishes the train moved faster' is also correct.)

(a) If wishes were horses, beggars would ride. (An imaginary condition in the past tense takes 'would'.)

(b) Should you visit Dehradun, you must stay with us. ('Should' at the start means 'if'.)

(c) You needn't go to him; a letter will do. (It is not necessary.)

(d) Kill the snake lest it should sting you. ('Lest' takes 'should'.)

(e) Our friends may turn into enemies. ('May' shows possibility; 'might' and 'could' are also possible.)

answers.finalAnswer: their servant had run away; if anything was missing; her gold watch was missing; she had kept it; was going to the police station to report it
answers.solution:
(a) their servant had run away
(b) if anything was missing
(c) her gold watch was missing
(d) she had kept it
(e) was going to the police station to report it

(In reported speech the tense moves one step back: 'has run away' becomes 'had run away', 'is' becomes 'was', 'did you keep' becomes 'she had kept', and 'am going' becomes 'was going'. A question becomes a statement introduced by 'if' or the question word.)
